hints: Identify all four forces acting on the 2.5 kg block: weight $mg = 25\text{ N}$ downwards, normal reaction $R$ perpendicular to the plane, tension $T$ at $20^\circ$ above the incline, and friction $F = \mu R$ acting down the incline.
Resolve forces perpendicular to the incline to find an expression for $R$ in terms of $T$: $R + T\sin 20^\circ = mg\cos 30^\circ$.
Resolve forces parallel to the incline for equilibrium: $T\cos 20^\circ = mg\sin 30^\circ + F$, and substitute $F = \frac{1}{4}R$.
Substitute the expression for $R$ into the parallel equation and solve the resulting linear equation for $T$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane in equilibrium:
$$R + T\sin 20^\circ = mg\cos 30^\circ = 2.5(10)\cos 30^\circ = 25\cos 30^\circ$$

Express the normal reaction $R$ in terms of $T$:
$$R = 25\cos 30^\circ - T\sin 20^\circ$$

Since the block is in limiting equilibrium about to move up the plane, friction acts down the plane with maximum value $F = \mu R$:
$$F = \frac{1}{4}R = 0.25(25\cos 30^\circ - T\sin 20^\circ)$$

Resolve forces parallel to the inclined plane in equilibrium:
$$T\cos 20^\circ = mg\sin 30^\circ + F = 25\sin 30^\circ + 0.25(25\cos 30^\circ - T\sin 20^\circ)$$

Rearrange to collect all terms in $T$ on the left-hand side:
$$T(\cos 20^\circ + 0.25\sin 20^\circ) = 25\sin 30^\circ + 6.25\cos 30^\circ$$

Substitute the numerical trigonometric values and solve for $T$:
$$T(0.93969 + 0.08551) = 12.5 + 5.41266 \implies 1.0252 T = 17.9127 \implies T = 17.5\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: First, list the forces acting on the $2.5\text{ kg}$ block. The weight is $W = mg = 2.5 \times 10 = 25\text{ N}$. The slope is inclined at $30^\circ$, and the tension $T$ acts at $20^\circ$ above the slope.

Set up the condition for equilibrium perpendicular to the inclined plane. The normal reaction $R$ and the perpendicular component of tension $T\sin 20^\circ$ balance the perpendicular component of weight:
$$R + T\sin 20^\circ = mg\cos 30^\circ$$

Substitute $m = 2.5\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$R + T\sin 20^\circ = 25\cos 30^\circ$$
$$R = 25\cos 30^\circ - T\sin 20^\circ$$

Because the block is about to move up the plane, limiting friction $F$ acts down the plane to oppose motion. Using $F = \mu R$ with $\mu = \frac{1}{4}$:
$$F = \frac{1}{4}\left(25\cos 30^\circ - T\sin 20^\circ\right)$$

Now resolve forces parallel to the plane. The upward pulling component $T\cos 20^\circ$ balances the downward component of weight plus friction:
$$T\cos 20^\circ = mg\sin 30^\circ + F$$

Substitute the expressions for weight and friction:
$$T\cos 20^\circ = 25\sin 30^\circ + \frac{1}{4}(25\cos 30^\circ - T\sin 20^\circ)$$

Expand the right-hand side and group the $T$ terms on the left:
$$T\cos 20^\circ + \frac{1}{4}T\sin 20^\circ = 25\sin 30^\circ + \frac{25}{4}\cos 30^\circ$$
$$T\left(\cos 20^\circ + 0.25\sin 20^\circ\right) = 12.5 + 6.25\cos 30^\circ$$

Evaluate the numbers: $\cos 20^\circ \approx 0.93969$, $\sin 20^\circ \approx 0.34202$, so $0.25\sin 20^\circ \approx 0.08551$. Thus the coefficient of $T$ is:
$$0.93969 + 0.08551 = 1.0252$$

Calculate the right-hand side using $\cos 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.86603$:
$$12.5 + 6.25(0.86603) = 12.5 + 5.4127 = 17.9127\text{ N}$$

Divide both sides by $1.0252$ to find $T$:
$$T = \frac{17.9127}{1.0252} \approx 17.472 \approx 17.5\text{ N}$$
